messages:
morgan: ran nsys on the small-batch steady load (1-4 reqs) on the G5 pool. noticing frequent short queue spikes that dominate tail latency.

sasha: can you paste the nsys command + a short tl;dr?

morgan: ```
nsys profile -o trace_miniwindow --trace=cuda,osrt --sample=none --duration=30s \n  --capture-range=kernel --cuda-graph-mode=none ./run_inference --batch_window_ms=25
```

morgan: top timeline snippet (aggregated by kernel):
```
kernel            calls  total_ms  avg_ms
fwd_attention     1024   920.5     0.899
gemm_fp16         2048   430.2     0.210
softmax_cuda      1024   120.8     0.118
kv_cache_lookup   512    48.6      0.095
kv_cache_write    512    22.8      0.044
```

morgan: but the full trace shows lots of tiny gaps between kernels: queue_time spikes in the 0.8-3ms range while compute per-kernel is 0.5-1.2ms. in many short-seq requests queue > compute.

kai: that's interesting — our continuous batching window is 25ms but it flushes early for prefixes. could this be scheduler preemption or a mutex stall? any perfetto nvprof data?

morgan: perfetto flame shows scheduling gaps aligned with CPU thread context switches. quick aggregate:
```
[GPU timeline] -> kernel | queue(wait) | kernel | idle
% time: compute 62%  queue+overhead 30%  idle 8%
```

sasha: kv cache behavior? hit vs miss?

morgan: hit rate ~96% for this workload, but writes cluster. writes take the cache lock and cause serialization: bursts of kv_cache_write correspond with queue accumulation across subsequent requests.

lin: @morgan can you try bumping KV writer threads to 4 and lowering batch_window_ms to 12ms as an experiment?

morgan: tried both on canary: lowered window -> tail P99 from 185ms -> 132ms. KV writer threads =4 reduced write stall tail but throughput dropped ~2.5%. so latency improved at modest throughput cost.

sasha: good initial data. sounds like a classic latency vs throughput tradeoff. maybe make window heuristic-based: short sequences get smaller window. also consider async cache writes to avoid holding the critical path.

kai: also saw a kernel-selection regression around commit ab3f2c: some short-seq paths fell back to gemm_fp16 launch path (higher kernel-launch overhead) instead of fused_gemm. forcing fused_gemm improved P99 by ~7ms in tests. can we add a guard to prefer fused kernels when seq_len < 128?

morgan: forced fused_gemm locally -> P99 improved 7ms. created a tiny config guard in runtime to prefer fused for seq<128. will PR.

profiler-bot: nsys summary for trace_miniwindow: total compute 62%, queue/overhead 30%, idle 8%. post-change (window=12 + KV threads=4 + fused guard) queue time reduced ~40% in tail. trace id: trace/1769200001.

sasha: next steps: 1) prototype async KV writer (offload writes to background batcher) 2) implement seq-len window heuristic (12ms for <64, 16ms for <128, 25ms otherwise) 3) patch kernel-picker to prefer fused_gemm on short seqs 4) re-run perfetto/nsys on canary and compare.

morgan: i'll open tickets and attach traces + nsys/perfetto links. adding screenshots to the ticket. thanks :thumbsup:

kai: one more ask — can we add a tiny perf counter in runtime that emits per-request queue_time vs compute_time so we can monitor these regressions without full traces? would help SLO alerts.

morgan: agreed — adding a lightweight metric (gpu_queue_ms, gpu_compute_ms) to emit via telemetry. will include in PR.

sasha: perfect. closing the loop once we have canary results.
